newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS says June traffic up 5.6 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: SAS says June traffic up 5.6 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said on Tuesday that its passenger traffic rose by 5.6 percent in June 1997, compared to June 1996.
"(There was) continued strong growth on the European, intra-Scandinavian and Norwegian domestic routes, the development of intercontinental traffic is positive," a SAS statement said.
"The Swedish and Danish domestic markets show some signs of improvement," it added.
It said it showed capacity growth of 2.6 percent over the same period.

Intra-Scandinavian traffic was the strongest performer, with growth of 13.1 percent, while the weakest was Greenland, Denmark's North Atlantic territory, with -0.2 percent growth, followed by Sweden with -0.9 percent.
SAS is jointly owned by the governments of Denmark, Norway and Sweden and by private investors.
It has come under increasing competition of late in its lucrative Scandinavian home market. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
